title: A Gravel Bike Finder Tool
text:
This site is designed to find the set of bikes that match the specifications you want in a frame. The focus is frame geometry, but there are also filters for material, suspension correction, UDH compatibility, sliding dropout, handlebar (flat or drop), axle spacing, maximum tire width, cost, and more.
This site classifies gravel bikes into Racy, Relaxed, and Rowdy styles based on their frame geometry. This is somewhat unique – most websites or podcasts that I know of categorize gravel bikes as “more racy” or “more mountain bikey”
Also…some hardtail mountain bikes are included because some hardtails make really good gravel bikes.

title: What makes a racy frame racy?
text:
Tip




Hover over data for model and frame size identification.
Scroll legend and click on items to identify specific model and frame size combinations.
Click on popup icon-bar over legend to zoom in/out and pan.









Note



Classification of gravel bikes is based on a frame size that fits a 175 cm high rider (generally frame size M or 54), according to manufacturer’s charts.



Racy bike frames have a combination of low stack, short front-center, high head tube angles, and low trail




















Racy frames have short reach, relative to rowdy frames








Racy frames have short chainstays (and rear-center), relative to relaxed frames








Racy frames can have low seat tube angles








Racy frames tend to have short front and rear centers. Relaxed frames tend to have long front and rear centers. So both racy and relaxed frames have low front-center:rear-center but for different reasons.








Stack:Reach and bottom brack drop aren’t really related to relaxedness

A Rudy Fork geometry corrector

Is your frame suspension corrected?
